transcript_text:
Meeting: Mid-pilot performance scrub — SummitBridge Health
Date/Time: 2027-07-22 15:30 UTC | Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE); Diego Morales (Redwood SE); Priya Nair (CTO, SummitBridge); Liam O'Connor (ML Eng); Sarah Tan (Infra)

Summary:
Quick mid-pilot readout comparing Redwood pilot runs vs their incumbent baseline for latency and throughput. Main topics: p95/p99 tail latency, steady-state QPS and concurrency, impact of batching and KV cache, fallback routing behavior, and potential need for a short dedicated slot trial. Action items include logs export, additional load tests, and sharing a routing/playbook doc.

Topics:
- p95/p99 latency deltas vs baseline provider
- Throughput (QPS) at target 2k and burst 5k levels
- Routing decisions (fallback to cheaper model variant)
- Caching/kv cache warmup and prefix hit rates
- Quantization and unit cost tradeoffs
- Next steps: dedicated slot trial, security handoff, contract draft

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: okay hi everyone thanks for joining on time, uh we wanted to run through the mid pilot -- the performance scrub, I know we had the lab runs earlier this week, diego you want to kick off with the numbers?
[00:23] Diego Morales: yeah sure, um quick preface — these numbers are from the 10k synthetic run on tuesday against the same prompt set you sent. we did two main configs: 1) Redwood hosted general-purpose route (quantized medium profile) and 2) Redwood dedicated slot (reserved GPU 80% p50 optimization). baseline is the incumbent provider's endpoint you gave us.
[00:48] Liam O'Connor: yeah just to be clear the baseline we provided is their prod-like endpoint, not a scaled-down test, so numbers should be representative.
[00:55] Diego Morales: good call. so for p95 latency: baseline averaged 420ms, Redwood hosted config averaged 360ms — so roughly 14% improvement. p99: baseline 1.6s, Redwood hosted 1.1s — that's a 31% improvement in tail.
[01:20] Priya Nair: wait 1.1 seconds p99? that seems optimistic, in our dev runs we saw some spikes closer to 2s still. are you including cold-starts?
[01:29] Diego Morales: we filtered cold starts; the run was warm after 150 requests, but you are right we still saw occasional spikes when the KV cache evicted for very long histories. those spikes were more frequent in the hosted general-profile.
[01:45] Sarah Tan: what's your warmup strategy for kv cache? like how long until prefix hits stabilize? we've seen different behavior when prompts are highly variable.
[01:54] Diego Morales: great question. for this workload with median sequence length ~320 tokens your prefix hit rate hit ~82% after 8 minutes. with longer tails it can drop to 60%. the dedicated slot config keeps the KV cache pinned and maintained, so tail spikes drop a lot.
[02:15] Maya Chen: to add, one of the leverages here is routing. we can route short requests to a cheaper quantized variant with similar quality and long-history requests to the dedicated or higher-memory instance to avoid evictions.
[02:30] Liam O'Connor: can you quantify cost change if we route 30% to quantized-variant? our procurement needs a delta estimate vs incumbent.
[02:38] Diego Morales: eyeballing from the runs, unit token cost drops ~22% if 30% goes to the quantized path, but latency p99 for those quantized requests is slightly higher — around 20% increase for long-context cases. so it's a tradeoff.
[02:56] Priya Nair: our priority is tail latency for interactive clinician flows, cost second. but we also can't exceed our monthly committed spend.
[03:06] Maya Chen: totally noted. on throughput — target was steady 2k QPS?
[03:11] Diego Morales: that was QPS as in 2k requests per minute? sorry we had a bit of mismatch. we tuned to 2k requests per minute which is ~33rps, our stress test included bursts up to 5k rpm (~83rps).
[03:27] Sarah Tan: yes, our SLAs are framed in RPS at percentile windows, so please keep both.
[03:33] Diego Morales: understood. at steady 33rps we saw no queuing and median latency at 220ms for Redwood hosted, baseline median was 260ms. at burst ~83rps the baseline showed a pronounced queue increase and p99 shot to 2.8s; Redwood hosted p99 stayed closer to 1.2–1.6s but only when KV cache warm.
[03:58] Liam O'Connor: were you using continuous batching? we see that changes behavior a lot.
[04:02] Diego Morales: yes continuous batching enabled for both our runs; we also varied max_batch_size: 8 vs 16. increasing batch size to 16 improved throughput by ~12% but added ~30ms median latency. so there's a sweet spot at 8/10 for your distribution.
[04:20] Priya Nair: Diego, did you run any 1:1 head-to-head with incumbents using identical prompt sets and sequence-length buckets?
[04:27] Diego Morales: we did 3 buckets (short, med, long). short (<128 tokens) Redwood and baseline comparable; medium (128–512) Redwood pulled ahead p95 by ~80ms; long (>512) Redwood dedicated had the biggest advantage because of less KV evictions.
[04:46] Maya Chen: one note on the long context: if you pin a dedicated slot we can set higher kv cache reserves and pin the model weights which really reduces the p99 spikes.
[04:58] Sarah Tan: are there infra implications? we run in a VPC and have strict egress rules. how do dedicated slots work with our networking?
[05:07] Maya Chen: good question — for Dedicated we offer VPC peering or private link. there's a short setup, and Diego can share the networking checklist. it integrates with your KMS for key management and logs export.
[05:20] Sarah Tan: okay please share checklist.
[05:23] Diego Morales: noted — I'll attach the VPC/private link checklist and steps.
[05:27] Priya Nair: back to numbers, what's the unit cost delta when you factor reserved capacity discounts?
[05:33] Diego Morales: with reserved (monthly commit) you can get ~30-40% off per-token compared to on-demand hosted. versus the incumbent, our committed pricing put unit cost about 12% lower given the same quantization profile. but your actual depends on profile and prefix hit rates.
[05:49] Liam O'Connor: can you surface token-level breakdowns per route? our finance team wants a per-route P&L.
[05:55] Diego Morales: yes we'll export a per-route token-cost table and include estimated monthly spend for the sample traffic mix.
[06:02] Maya Chen: quick aside, did the baseline show any consistent tail reasons? like garbage collection on their side or load-shedding?
[06:10] Liam O'Connor: their monitoring is opaque, but we do detect occasional queue rejections and increased CPU on their host during bursts. not sure about GC but looks like they scale reactively.
[06:20] Diego Morales: that reactive scaling explains the longer tails. Redwood's smart routing and burst buffer aims to smooth that.
[06:26] Priya Nair: Any notes on accuracy/quality regressions from quantized variants? we can't accept degraded clinician-facing summaries.
[06:35] Diego Morales: we ran our eval harness against the prompt set. quantized-medium had negligible BLEU-like deltas for summaries; there were edge cases on numeric table extraction where we prefer the higher-precision variant. recommended: route extractive/structured prompts to higher-fidelity path.
[06:55] Maya Chen: that routing can be automated — function-call or structured output detection and then route to a fidelity path automatically.
[07:03] Sarah Tan: excellent. can Redwood run a 24-hour soak on dedicated slot so we can observe cache behavior over day/night shift?
[07:11] Diego Morales: yes we can schedule a 24–48 hour soak on a dedicated slot. it helps us tune autoscaling thresholds and eviction windows.
[07:20] Liam O'Connor: what's the friction to move from hosted to dedicated in mid-pilot? do we need a contract?
[07:25] Maya Chen: we can offer a short-term reserved slot (30 days) pilot with a light contract addendum — Diego will draft the sizing options and estimate costs.
[07:33] Priya Nair: and if we find regressions in the quantized route, what's the rollback process?
[07:38] Diego Morales: we have immediate routing fallback policies — you can configure automatic fallback to higher-fidelity models or to baseline in worst case. we can also do canary percentages.
[07:47] Liam O'Connor: can we see a sample rollback policy?
[07:50] Diego Morales: yes I'll share the playbook doc.
[07:53] Maya Chen: switching to tail analysis — we pulled a p99 trace and noticed most spikes correlated to requests with long context plus plugin-style structured function calls, which forces larger KV operations.
[08:05] Priya Nair: that's our clinical note generation flow, typically 900–1.2k token contexts.
[08:10] Diego Morales: okay for those we recommend dedicated slot or a higher memory host; also setting a longer eviction window for KV cache reduces tail frequency but increases memory usage. it's a tradeoff.
[08:22] Sarah Tan: how much memory increase? ballpark numbers?
[08:25] Diego Morales: for your median it's ~15–20% extra RAM to raise eviction window by 2x for the dataset we saw.
[08:33] Priya Nair: that's acceptable if it smooths p99. we care about 99.9th more than cost for clinician flows.
[08:40] Maya Chen: noted. next up, question about tooling — do you want token-level cost dashboards routed into your Splunk/Datadog?
[08:47] Liam O'Connor: yes Datadog. we already ingest traces there.
[08:50] Diego Morales: we can stream per-request traces and token breakdowns to Datadog via our tracing hooks, we'll include a sample dashboard.
[08:59] Priya Nair: great. regarding security, Sarah will own the SSO/KMS discussion.
[09:04] Sarah Tan: yes, timeline wise we prefer that before we do dedicated slot trial. next step is a 1-hour security handoff.
[09:11] Maya Chen: we'll set that up.
[09:13] Liam O'Connor: another small datapoint — we saw a 7% accuracy regression on structured numeric extraction with quantized-high variant in a small eval slice. is that expected?
[09:23] Diego Morales: quantization can cause small numeric diffs; for structured numeric extraction we recommend either fallback to high-precision model or post-processing validation checks.
[09:32] Priya Nair: ok agree.
[09:34] Maya Chen: action item recap — Diego export per-route cost table, routing playbook, VPC checklist; Liam provide prompt set and lengths; Maya send contract draft; Sarah schedule security handoff.
[09:47] Diego Morales: quick note — in the export I'll also include warm cache metrics by minute so you can see eviction windows.
[09:55] Priya Nair: perfect. any blockers on Redwood side?
[10:00] Diego Morales: none. we may request temporary elevated logging during soak.
[10:05] Sarah Tan: okay we'll enable logs.
[10:08] Maya Chen: timeline proposal: dedicated 48-hour soak starting 2027-07-31, papers exchanged by 2027-07-30, security handoff week of 2027-08-02, follow-up readout 2027-08-05. does that work?
[10:23] Priya Nair: works for us pending contract review.
[10:26] Liam O'Connor: yep good.
[10:28] Maya Chen: any final questions?
[10:31] Priya Nair: none from me. thanks.
[10:34] Sarah Tan: thanks.
[10:36] Diego Morales: thanks all, will follow up with docs and exports.

End of meeting.

Notes / Imperfections: occasional mis-heard product names in the automated transcription (e.g., "Redwood dedicate"), timestamps approximate, speaker tags on a couple lines were genericized. References to shared artifacts: "routing_playbook_v2.pdf" (we will attach), "per-route-costs.csv" and a Datadog dashboard link will be shared in follow-up.
